Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act. Please contact the City Clerk at (310) 378-0383, at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
Any person who has made campaign contributions to any of the members of the Planning Commission within twelve months before this meeting, should examine the provisions of Government Code Section 84308 which is posted on the bulletin board outside the Council Chamber.
We are advised by the members of the Commission that none of them have received campaign contributions within the last twelve months.
The applicant or any property owner entitled to notice of the hearing may, within fifteen days after the date of the Planning Commission decision, appeal the Planning Commission decision to the City Council (Ord. No. 091-529). A fee is required for filing an appeal with the City Clerkâ€™s office (R05-14).
The Council may, within fifteen days after the date of the decision or on or before the first date following the first Council meeting after the date of the Planning Commission decision, whichever occurs last: 1) Confirm the action of the Planning Commission and grant or deny the application; 2) Set the matter for public hearing and dispose of it in the same manner as on an appeal; or 3) Amend, modify, delete or add any condition of approval which the Council finds is not substantial under the circumstances relative to or affecting the property subject to the application for a development entitlement. Any determination of the Council pursuant to this paragraph shall be conclusive and final.
The Planning Commission reserves the right to modify the order of items shown on the agenda and advises all interested parties to arrive promptly at the commencement of the meeting.

MINUTES OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES,
  CALIFORNIA

  January 19, 2016

  A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Palos Verdes Estates was
called to order by Chair Thomas at 6:00 p.m. on January 19, 2016, in the City Council
Chambers, 340 Palos Verdes Drive West, Palos Verdes Estates, California. The Pledge of
Allegiance followed.

ROLL CALL

Present:  Kao, Evans, Hunter, Welch, Chair Thomas

Absent:  None

Also Present: Planning Director Repp-Loadsman; City Planner Corpuz; City Assistant City
  Attorney Kettles

  *  *  *

COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

None.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Chair Thomas, upon confirmation the applicants present understood the suggested conditions of
approval, opened the public hearing, confirmed that there were no interested persons wishing to
voice concerns regarding the application considered for the Consent Calendar, and closed the
public hearing.

1.  M-1076-16; Consideration of a Miscellaneous Application for a new detached structure
  exceeding the allowable height at the single family residence located at 3657 Navajo
  Place. Lot 4 & a portion of Lot 5, Block 6104, Tract 6887. This project is exempt from
  CEQA pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303

  Applicant/Owner:  Carl & Anke Campanella

MOTION

  Commissioner Kao moved to approve M-1076-16 for 3657 Navajo Place, exempt from
CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning Resolution PCR-2016-0899 with
standard conditions and the following additional condition: 1) The proposed play structure shall
be setback a minimum of 5 ft. to the side property line and a minimum of 5 ft. from the rear

Planning Commission  1  January 19, 2016
 property line. The motion was seconded by Commissioner Welch and was carried by unanimous
oral vote.

2.  NC-1544-15; Consideration of a Neighborhood Compatibility Application for additions
  and remodeling to the single family residence located at 4137 Via Solano. Lot 18, Block
  6317, Tract 7143. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to California
  Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant:  Brian Noteware
  2850 Ocean Park Blvd., #315
  Santa Monica, CA 90405

  Owner:  Michael & Nancy Keating

MOTION

  Commissioner Kao moved to approve NC-1544-15 for 4137 Via Solano, exempt from
CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning Resolution PCR-2015-0874 with
standard conditions and the following additional condition: 1) All non-standard encroachments
shall be removed including, but not limited to, the stepping stones within the City right-of-way.
The motion was seconded by Commissioner Welch and was carried by unanimous oral vote.

3.  NC-1545-15; Consideration of a Neighborhood Compatibility Application for a new
  single family residence located at 4008 Via Cardelina. Lot 17, Block 6310, Tract 7143.
  This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14,
  Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant:  Russ Barto
  3 Malaga Cove Plaza, #202
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

  Owner:  Adam & Stephanie Felenstein

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Russ Barto (3 Malaga Cove Plaza) came forward and presented the application.

Mark Shreckengast (4009 Via Gavilan) came forward with privacy concerns with the deck off of
the new master bedroom looking directly into his backyard and home.

Mr. Barto re-approached and said that this issue could be taken care of by screen planting and
offered to reduce the depth of the deck.

Discussion ensued among the Commissioners and Mr. Barto regarding the master bedroom and
deck design.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Planning Commission  2  January 19, 2016
 Commissioner Kao discussed screening and landscaping as a visual and audio hedge and asked
about requirements of enforceable landscaping, and Planning Director Repp-Loadsman advised
that the City is always hesitant to monitor landscaping advised being mindful of the Los Angeles
County Fire Department regulations.

Commissioner Kao suggested the landscaping issue could be between the Homes Association
and private parties and asked about brokering deals between neighbors, and City Attorney
Kettles suggested that a permit with conditions be issued regarding landscape maintenance.

Commissioner Evans commented that he supports the applicant’s suggestions, such as making
the deck smaller and providing screen planting along the property line.

Commissioner Welch agreed.

Commissioner Kao suggested a continuance to allow time to visit the Shreckengast property.

Commissioner Welch commented that the application is approvable if the applicant modifies the
deck size and installs the landscaping.

Chair Thomas stated that the deck wouldn’t create a privacy impact, but he could agree to the
modifications and asked for specifics on the landscape screening.

Planning Director Repp-Loadsman recommended that the applicant provide landscaping along
the rear property line.

Commissioner Welch and City Planner Corpuz discussed fencing between the properties.

MOTION

  Commissioner Hunter moved to approve NC-1545-15 for 4008 Via Cardelina, exempt
from CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning Resolution PCR-2015-0874
with standard conditions and the following additional conditions: 1) The depth of the second
story master bedroom deck shall be revised to be 5 ft.; 2) Landscaping shall be provided along
the rear property line to provide a visual barrier between the subject property and the property to
the rear at 4009 Via Gavilan. A landscape plan shall be submitted and reviewed and approved
by the Planning Director. The motion was seconded by Commissioner Welch and was carried by
unanimous oral vote.

OLD BUSINESS

4.  NC-1541/G-1559/M-1053/M-1066-15; Consideration of Neighborhood Compatibility,
  Grading & Miscellaneous Applications for a new single family residence located at 2812
  Victoria Place. Lot 16, Block 2450, Tract 7332. This project is exempt from CEQA
  pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant:  Rosa Velazquez
  118 S. Catalina Ave., #N
  Redondo Beach, CA 90277

Planning Commission  3  January 19, 2016
   Owner:  Ebrahim Soltani

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

Rosa Velazquez (118 S. Catalina Avenue, Redondo Beach) came forward and presented the
application.

Discussion ensued among the Commission and Ms. Velazquez regarding the new landscaping
plan, revisions to the plans, air conditioning units and chimney/deck placements.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Jeanne and Fikret Atamdede (2818 Victoria Place) came forward and expressed their concerns
regarding loss of privacy due to elevations, the pool deck and window placement.

Leven Leatherbury (2729 Palos Verdes Drive West) came forward and discussed his issues with
the pool deck and his added concern about the height of the trellis inhibiting privacy.

Ms. Velazquez re-approached, spoke about changing the existing landscaping to provide privacy,
commented on the existing trellis grade, and proposed building another lower fence on the deck.
Ms. Velazquez pointed out that the higher fence is temporary until the growth of new trees is
complete and that the perimeter footprint elevations are being maintained on the front and back
of the property.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Commissioner Kao asked about placement of the air conditioning units, and City Planner Corpuz
answered that air conditioning units cannot be placed in any setback and that based on the plans
they are outside of the setback lines and in compliance.

The Commissioners addressed the privacy issues and agreed that the application cannot be
approved as submitted.

CONTINUED TO THE FEBRUARY 16, 2016 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING.

5.  NC-1543/G-1560/M-1064/M-1065-15; Consideration of Neighborhood Compatibility,
  Grading & Miscellaneous Applications for a new single family residence located at 709
  Via Somonte. Lot 11, Block 1538, Tract 6884. This project is exempt from CEQA
  pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Owner:  GA Design Inc.

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

Commissioner Hunter and City Planner Corpuz discussed nonstandard encroachment elevations
pertaining to planter placement.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Mahmoud Gharachedaghi (architect at GA Design Architecture and Planning, 19191 S. Vermont
Avenue, #640, Torrance) came forward and presented the application.

Planning Commission  4  January 19, 2016
 Commissioner Kao and Mr. Gharachedaghi discussed the garage height, and Mr. Gharachedaghi
advised that he is opposed to lowering the garage height mainly because of the expense involved.

Elaine and Rick Bohner (793 Via Somonte), Anthony Greger (736 Via Somonte), Jim Kinney
(721 Via Somonte), John Dixon (641 Via Del Monte), Derek Lazzaro (804 Via Somonte),
Richard Dennen (813 Via Somonte), Fred Gregory (816 Via Somonte) and Gerry Brooke (812
Via Somonte) all came forward in opposition to the project due to the height of the property,
invasion of privacy, obstructed views, height of future vegetation, lot size, precedent and access
to fire trucks and garbage trucks.

Stephanie Streisand (705 Via Somonte) came forward in favor of the project, stating that the
applicant has made compromises and should be allowed to develop his home.

Mr. Gharachedaghi re-approached and commented that based on Planning Commission and
neighbor recommendations he has changed the design and height of the project several times.
Mr. Gharachedaghi then discussed the building style and scale in comparison to surrounding
homes.

The Commissioners and Mr. Gharachedaghi discussed the Bohners’ three specific suggestions in
regard to reducing the height.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Commissioner Welch, Planning Director Repp-Loadsman and City Planner Corpuz discussed
maximum height limits regarding retaining walls.

Commissioner Hunter reviewed pictures submitted by Mr. and Mrs. Bohner and stated that with
their suggested roof height compromise the issue will be resolved.

Commissioner Kao disagreed and stated that the project should have been denied from the
beginning.

Commissioner Welch commended Mr. Kinney for his input, stated that the project is close to
approval and he agreed with the roof height reduction.

Commissioner Evans commended the applicant for his compromises but added that there are still
more compromises to be made.

Chair Thomas reiterated that that this is the most impactful project he has seen and agreed that
the roofline can be lowered.

Commissioners Welch and Hunter and Chair Thomas agreed that they need to see a final
revision before approving.

CONTINUED TO THE FEBRUARY 16, 2016 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING.

Planning Commission  5  January 19, 2016
 NEW BUSINESS

6.  WT-135-15; Wireless Telecommunication Facilities Application for new equipment
  within the City right-of-way across from 1428 Paseo La Cresta.

  Applicant:  Crown Castle NG West LLC
  300 Spectrum Center Dr., #1200
  Irvine, CA 92618

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

Commissioner Kao and City Planner Corpuz discussed the timing of filing of the application and
review by the Planning Commission.

Jonathan Kramer (wireless consultant at 2001 S Barrington Ave, Los Angeles) came forward.
Chair Thomas and Mr. Kramer discussed approval methods available for this application.
Commissioner Kao and Mr. Kramer discussed distance proximities and topography.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Steven Garcia (Crown Castle NG West LLC, 300 Spectrum Center Drive, Irvine) came forward
and presented the application.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Commissioner Evans, Kao, Hunter and Welch and Chair Thomas all agreed to approve the
application.

MOTION

  Commissioner Kao moved to approve WT-135-15 within the City right-of-way across
from 1428 Paseo La Cresta, exempt from CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in
Planning Resolution PCR-2015-0880 with standard conditions and the following additional
conditions: 1) The steel pole shall be burnished prior to painting. The pole and antennas must be
painted a flat dark brown, and maintained in the same condition thereafter; 2) All cables
interconnecting the antennas and all transmission equipment should run within the replacement
pole except as minimally required to connect to the antennas; 3) The equipment cabinet should
be painted a color to blend in with the existing surrounding environment and nearby meter
cabinet in the PROW; 4) The replacement steel pole is not a wireless tower for any purpose, but
rather it is considered only a replacement City street sign pole; 5) The steel pole shall be
designated as a replacement for the existing pole to be removed, and after installation, the
replacement pole shall be dedicated to the City for a fee of $1.00 so that it is clear for federal law
purposes that replacement pole maintain its primary use and function as a City traffic sign
support; 6) Permittee shall install and at all times maintain in good condition an “RF Notice” and
“Network Operations Center Information” sign on the steel pole at approximately 14 feet AGL;
7) Permittee shall ensure that all RF signage complies with FCC OET Bulletin 65 or ANSI C95.2
for color, symbol, and content conventions; 8) Attached one way sign shall be installed in
accordance with the MUTCD (Manual Uniform Traffic Control Devices) California Edition; and
9) Attached one way sign shall be with approved hardware per the City’s Maintenance Foreman.

Planning Commission  6  January 19, 2016
 City Planner Corpuz advised that Staff will prepare a resolution that indicates a denial. The
motion was seconded by Commissioner Evans and was carried by unanimous oral vote.

7.  WT-145-15; Wireless Telecommunication Facilities Application for new equipment
  within the City right-of-way across from 801 Via Coronel.

  Applicant:  Crown Castle NG West LLC
  300 Spectrum Center Dr., #1200
  Irvine, CA 92618u

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

Commissioner Hunter and City Planner Corpuz discussed the draft resolution incorporating the
figure 2 configuration.

Jonathan Kramer (wireless consultant at 2001 S Barrington Ave, Los Angeles) came forward.
Commissioner Kao and Mr. Kramer discussed topography and elevation change and radius of a
DAS site. Commissioner Evans and Mr. Kramer discussed summary offset antennas compared
to lined antennas.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Steven Garcia (Crown Castle NG West LLC, 300 Spectrum Center Drive, Irvine) came forward
and presented the application.

Chair Thomas and Mr. Garcia discussed ownership of the pole.

Dale Sanchez (744 Cloyden Road) and David Armitage (1809 Palos Verdes Drive West) came
forward in opposition to this project stating their desire to maintain beautiful neighborhood
views, objecting to unsightly telephone poles and claiming that the existing cell reception is
adequate. Mr. Armitage suggested dressing up the poles to match the neighborhood.

Chair Thomas asked Mr. Armitage whether the poles are in his view from his home, and
Mr. Armitage confirmed that they are.

Mary Ellen Seville (2200 Chelsea Road) came forward in opposition to this project due to her
residence already being impacted by the installation of a wire vault by Crown Castle.

Mr. Garcia re-approached to address the concerns raised by the neighbors and explained that the
coverage area is based on consumer activity monitored closely by AT&T and re-evaluated by
Crown Castle. The goal is to provide the fewest locations possible to provide the best coverage.
Mr. Garcia then discussed safety guidelines.

Commissioner Evans, Chair Thomas and Mr. Garcia discussed the possibility of moving the pole
back into existing landscaping or replacing the pole while maintaining the coverage objective.

Mr. Kramer re-approached, and Chair Thomas and Mr. Kramer discussed the effect of foliage on
poles and pole realignment.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Planning Commission  7  January 19, 2016
 Commissioners Hunter discussed the location of the pole and recommended moving it into the
right-of-way and using the taller pole without the DAS nodes.

Commissioners Kao, Hunter and Welch agreed to move the pole into the shrubbery.

Commissioner Evans disagreed, stating that it would be very noticeable and would change the
direction of the cable.

Chair Thomas added that moving the pole into the shrubbery would cause misalignment and
discussed exploring the options.

Mr. Kramer re-approached, discussed the two options proposed in the application and suggested
that Crown Castle perform a visual simulation on both.

Commissioners Kao, Hunter, Evans and Welch and Chair Thomas all agreed.

CONTINUED TO THE FEBRUARY 16, 2016 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING.

8.  NC-1539/G-1557/M-1079/M-1080-15; Consideration of Neighborhood Compatibility,
  Grading & Miscellaneous Applications for a new single family residence located at 2101
  Chelsea Rd. Lot 6, Block 2100, Tract 7331. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant
  to California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant:  Cauthen Design Inc.
  20141 E. Chapman Ave.
  Orange, CA 92869

  Owner:  Kirby & Sally Larson

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

Commissioner Welch and City Planner Corpuz discussed approved square footage for this
project.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Ben Cauthen (20141 East Chapman, Orange) came forward and presented the application.

Sally and Kirby Larson (owners at 2101 Chelsea Road) came forward and expressed their love
for the neighborhood and respect toward the adjoining neighbors.

Brent Celestin (2109 Thorley Road), Louis Zakin (2112 Chelsea Road), Clark Kasunich (2108
Chelsea Road) and Craig Stephens (2105 Thorley Road) all came forward in opposition to the
project due to square footage, neighborhood compatibility standards, view obstruction and
elevation.

Sally and Kirby Larson re-approached, discussed the size of the structure in comparison to
surrounding homes, expressed their willingness to compromise and modify the project design to
accommodate surrounding neighbors and gave some suggestions.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Planning Commission  8  January 19, 2016
 Commissioners Hunter, Kao, Welch, Evans and Chair Thomas all agreed that there needs to be
compromise and commended Mr. and Mrs. Larson on their willingness to compromise.

CONTINUED TO THE FEBRUARY 16, 2016 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING

9.  NC-1546/G-1561/M-1078-15; Consideration of Neighborhood Compatibility, Grading &
  Miscellaneous Applications for a new single family residence located at 960 Paseo La
  Cresta. Lot 9, Tract 31329. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to California
  Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant:  Tomaro Architecture
  2617 N. Sepulveda Blvd., #100
  Manhattan Beach, CA 90266

  Owner:  Prolina LLC
  2301 Via Acalones
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

Commissioner Welch and Planning Director Repp-Loadsman discussed the term “adversely
surcharge”.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Louie Tomaro (architect at 2617 N. Sepulveda Boulevard., Manhattan Beach) came forward and
presented the application.

Planning Director Repp-Loadsman commented on a handout provided by the applicant’s
representative concerning cross sections, and Mr. Tomaro advised that he would like to use the
photos for any rebuttal.

Commissioner Kao and Mr. Tomaro discussed ridge line modifications throughout the planning
process.

Chair Thomas and Mr. Tomaro discussed the reasoning for the large circular motor court.

Elaine and Morris Asch (955 Paseo La Cresta), Lydia and Todd Bauer (959 Paseo La Cresta) and
Chingmuh Lee (956 Paseo La Cresta) came forward in opposition to the project due to view
obstruction, square footage, plate heights, chimney design, change of quality of life, tennis court
restrictions, landslide hazards, grading issues, no cooperation from the applicants, privacy, value
of property and roof height issues.

Brad Dudley (architect at 345 3rd Street, Laguna Beach) came forward and discussed solutions to
preserving views.

Mr. Tomaro re-approached and addressed the issues raised and his proposed revisions.

Commissioner Hunter and Mr. Tomaro discussed chimney requirements.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Planning Commission  9  January 19, 2016
 Commissioner Hunter, Planning Director Repp-Loadsman and City Attorney Kettles discussed
decorative chimney and venting requirements.

Commissioner Hunter commented on the proposed home size and stated that the applicants need
to compromise with their neighbors.

Commissioner Welch stated that the applicant has compromised and made recommendations
about the vent gas appliances.

Commissioners Kao and Evans and Chair Thomas agreed with both Commissioners Hunter and
Welch and discussed privacy issues and possible resolutions.

CONTINUED TO THE FEBRUARY 16, 2016 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING

10.  NC-1547/G-1562/M-1077-15; Consideration of Neighborhood Compatibility, Grading &
  Miscellaneous Applications for a new single family residence located at 941 Via
  Nogales. Lot 1, Block 1633, Tract 7330. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to
  California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant:  Tomaro Architecture
  2617 N. Sepulveda Blvd., #100
  Manhattan Beach, CA 90266

  Owner:  Chowdhury Homes LLC
  32040 Cape Point Dr.
  Rancho Palos Verdes, CA 90275

CHAIR THOMAS RECUSED HIMSELF FROM THIS AGENDA ITEM.

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

COMMISSIONER EVANS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Louie Tomaro (2617 N. Sepulveda Boulevard, Manhattan Beach) came forward and presented
the application.

Commissioner Welch and Mr. Tomaro discussed the existing stone wall, city right-of-way,
driveway and flagging.

Commissioner Evans and Mr. Tomaro discussed Allan Singer (1005 Via Mirabel) being in favor
of the proposed project.

Commissioner Welch and Planning Director Repp-Loadsman discussed the city right-of-way and
non-conformity stemming from the adjoining property owner.

COMMISSIONER EVANS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Commissioner Hunter and Planning Director Repp-Loadsman discussed pathway access.

Commissioners Welch and Evans and City Planner Corpuz discussed a driveway gate.
Commissioner Welch commented that he will approve with the staff recommendations.

Planning Commission  10  January 19, 2016
 Commissioner Kao commented on project size relative to the neighborhood and stated that none
of the neighbors had any issues.

Commissioners Hunter and Evans agreed.

MOTION

  Commissioner Welch moved to approve NC-1547/G-1562/M-1077-15 for 941 Via
Nogales, exempt from CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning Resolution
PCR-2015-0894 with standard conditions and the following additional conditions: 1) Portions of
the lot being graded/excavated exceed 25% grade; thus, the project shall comply with the City’s
municipal NPDES permit and requirements set forth in Municipal Code 13.08.060, Section C; 2)
A license agreement shall be submitted to defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the city, its
officers, agents and employees from and against any and all loss, damage, liability, claims,
